title: The article discusses the challenges faced in famine-relief efforts in Africa, exacerbated by ongoing wars and a decline in global attention and aid. While the media focuses on crises in Eastern Europe and the Gulf, African famines have received less coverage and support. The end of the Cold War has diminished the strategic importance of African nations, leading to a decrease in aid programs. Additionally, the phenomenon of 'aid fatigue' has shifted fundraising efforts towards local causes in the West, leaving African famine relief underfunded and overlooked.
